- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

type.description: What kind of feedback this is.

title.description: Short, specific one-line summary of the issue.

details.description: Labeled bullets, in order: **What happened:** (observed vs. expected, exact error text if short); **What the user said:** (quoted, or "User didn't comment; observed by the model."); **Repro:** (minimal steps); **Evidence:** (request IDs, timestamps, paths, versions; omit if none); optionally a final **Cause:** only if verified in-session. One to three lines per bullet. No narrative paragraphs, no speculation, no secrets.

area.description: Optional short tag naming the part of Claude Code this is about (e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing"). Leave blank if unclear.

failure_mode.description: When the report is about MODEL BEHAVIOR (not a product bug), the closest failure mode, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value. Omit only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.

task_category.description: What kind of task the session was doing when the issue occurred, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: TaskStop
tools.description:
- Stops a running background task by its ID
- Takes a task_id parameter identifying the task to stop
- To stop an agent-team teammate, pass its agent ID or bare teammate name as task_id
- To stop a background agent spawned with a name, pass that name as task_id
- Returns a success or failure status
- Use this tool when you need to terminate a long-running task

task_id.description: The ID of the background task to stop. Agent-team teammates and named background agents are also accepted by agent ID or name.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: WebFetch
tools.description:
Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead. claude.ai artifact links (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}) are published artifacts: read them with the Artifact tool (action "read"), not WebFetch or curl.
- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

url.description: The URL to fetch content from

prompt.description: The prompt to run on the fetched content

offset.description: Character position in the page text to start reading from. Use it to read on through a page too long for one call, with the value the previous result gave.

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to write (must be absolute, not relative)

content.description: The content to write to the file

tools.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of browser tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — if an action navigates to a domain without permission, the next item's check fails and the batch stops. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested.

name.description: Tool name (e.g. computer, navigate, find, tabs_create_mcp). browser_batch cannot be nested.

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

actions.description: List of tool calls to execute sequentially. Example: [{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"left_click","coordinate":[100,200],"tabId":123}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"type","text":"hello","tabId":123}},{"name":"navigate","input":{"url":"https://example.com","tabId":123}}]

tools.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer
tools.description:
Use a mouse and keyboard to interact with a web browser, and take screenshots. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.
* Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element before moving the cursor.
* If you tried clicking on a program or link but it failed to load, even after waiting, try adjusting your click location so that the tip of the cursor visually falls on the element that you want to click.
* Make sure to click any buttons, links, icons, etc with the cursor tip in the center of the element. Don't click boxes on their edges unless asked.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported and will return an error - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels. Requires a Claude in Chrome extension version that supports scale; older extensions return the full-size image.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

tabId.description: Tab ID to execute the action on. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

save_to_disk.description: For screenshot/zoom actions: save the image to disk so it can be attached to a message for the user. Returns the saved path in the tool result. Only set this when you intend to share the image — screenshots you're just looking at don't need saving.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__find
tools.description: Find elements on the page using natural language. Can search for elements by their purpose (e.g., "search bar", "login button") or by text content (e.g., "organic mango product"). Returns up to 20 matching elements with references that can be used with other tools. If more than 20 matches exist, you'll be notified to use a more specific query. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

query.description: Natural language description of what to find (e.g., "search bar", "add to cart button", "product title containing organic")

tabId.description: Tab ID to search in. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

tools.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__form_input
tools.description: Set values in form elements using element reference ID from the read_page tool. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

ref.description: Element reference ID from the read_page tool (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2")

value.description: The value to set. For checkboxes use boolean, for selects use option value or text, for other inputs use appropriate string/number

tabId.description: Tab ID to set form value in. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this form fill does on the page and to what, for example 'Sets the delivery date to 29 September'. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__get_page_text
tools.description: Extract raw text content from the page, prioritizing article content. Ideal for reading articles, blog posts, or other text-heavy pages. Returns plain text without HTML formatting. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

tabId.description: Tab ID to extract text from. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

---
name: Entire-Checkpoint trailer in every commit
description: When making git commits in sc4sap_project, MUST include `Entire-Checkpoint: <id>` trailer to keep entire session tracking intact
type: feedback
originSessionId: 21e03650-294e-4f69-aaef-74c569183474
modified: 2026-09-29T23:29:06.682Z
---
When creating any `git commit` in `sc4sap_project` (or any repo where `entire` is enabled), the commit message MUST include an `Entire-Checkpoint: <id>` trailer in the trailer block (next to / below `Co-Authored-By:`).

**Why:** `entire attach <session-id>` only registers checkpoint metadata in entire's DB and prints "Copy to your commit message to attach: Entire-Checkpoint: <id>". It does NOT automatically amend the commit to add the trailer (because last commit may already be pushed). The trailer is the chain mechanism — without it on a commit, entire's session ↔ commit linkage breaks for that commit and every subsequent one in the chain.

**How to apply:**
- Before authoring a commit, run `entire sessions list` (or `entire status`) and grab the active session's `checkpoint <id>` field.
- Append `Entire-Checkpoint: <id>` as a trailer line in the commit message, on its own line in the trailer block.
- Reuse the same checkpoint ID for every commit in the same Claude Code session — `entire attach` only mints a new checkpoint when there's no checkpoint registered for the session yet.
- If the project active branch is shared (NO force-push policy) and a commit was already pushed without the trailer, do NOT try to fix via `entire attach` afterwards — it will `git commit --amend` the last commit silently and rewrite hash, forcing a reset-to-origin to recover.

**Real incident (2026-04-26):** Commit 1f4c5bf (program-to-spec PNG path fix) was authored without the trailer despite user having run `entire attach 21e03650...` earlier in the session. Result: trailer-less commit pushed to active/backup/main, and a follow-up `entire attach` silently amended local 1f4c5bf → f7615b7 forcing a hash divergence that had to be reset (force-push blocked by shared-branch policy). Net effect: that commit is permanently un-tracked by entire on origin.

**Safe pattern when the session has no checkpoint yet (worked 2026-09-30):** commit first (unpushed), then `entire attach <session-id> -f` — it amends only that unpushed commit with the trailer and mints the checkpoint; reuse the ID for later commits/merge. Never attach while HEAD is an already-pushed commit.

Quick template for commits in this project:
```
<type>(<scope>): <subject>

<body>

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Entire-Checkpoint: <fetch via `entire sessions list`>
```

Update 2026-10-20: for a session not captured by hooks, `entire attach <session-id> -f` creates the checkpoint AND amends the last commit with the `Entire-Checkpoint:` trailer. Use it only while that commit is unpushed (active is shared: no amend-push). Used for 42245ae.

content.text:
두 문제를 고쳤고, 백엔드 npm도 올려서 커밋 8개를 푸시했어요.

**1. 드래그하면 페이지가 같이 움직이던 문제**
- 원인은 브라우저의 스크롤 앵커링이었어요. 브라우저가 그래프 안 글자를 기준점으로 잡아서, 그래프를 끌면 페이지도 그만큼 스크롤됐어요.
- 그래프 영역을 기준점에서 뺐어요.
- 페이지를 내린 상태에서 드래그해 봤어요. 그래프만 움직이고 페이지는 그대로였어요.

**2. 검색에 ZSDR24730A가 나오던 문제**
- 이 PROG들은 소스를 가져온 적도 없고 관계도 없어요. 그래프에서 뺐어요.
  - 대부분 어디서도 쓰지 않는 INCLUDE예요. ZSDR24730F는 메인 프로그램 30번째 줄에서 주석 처리돼 있어요.
  - ZSD400에서 55개가 빠졌어요.
- 이제 `ZSDR24730`을 검색하면 프로그램과 TCode만 나와요.
- 이 확인은 스크립트로 했어요. 중간에 Chrome 확장 연결이 끊겨서 화면으로는 못 봤어요.

**3. 백엔드 npm 업데이트**
- Agent SDK는 0.3.223에서 0.3.304로 올렸어요.
- Anthropic SDK는 0.115에서 0.135로 올렸어요.
- MCP SDK, fastify, mongodb, zod, tsx도 최신으로 올렸어요.
- 보안 경고 5개를 고쳐서 0개가 됐어요. 치명적인 것(`proxy-addr`)도 하나 있었어요.
- 메이저 버전 두 개는 일부러 올리지 않았어요.
  - TypeScript 7은 컴파일러를 새로 작성한 버전이에요.
  - @types/node 26은 지금 Node 24 런타임과 맞지 않아요.
- 타입 검사는 통과했어요. 서버도 새 패키지로 정상 기동했어요.
- 채팅 한 번을 실제로 주고받는 테스트는 아직 안 했어요. API 비용이 들어서요.

**푸시**
- `feat/session-ownership`에 `b4ec28a`까지 올렸어요. 이제 남은 로컬 커밋은 없어요.

Chrome 확장이 다시 연결되면 다음 이슈를 알려주세요.

name: project/sc4sap/vendor/abap-mcp-adt — editing forbidden
description: sc4sap project vendor/ is a bridge-bootstrap dev clone, not a source-of-truth; edit only marketplaces/abap-mcp-adt-powerup and mirror outward
type: feedback
originSessionId: 0f8d75a1-19fc-415f-890e-3d9ef52c9de8
`C:/Users/pssps/Documents/Projects/sc4sap_project/sc4sap/vendor/abap-mcp-adt/` is **NOT** a source of truth. Do not edit files there. The MCP server source-of-truth is `~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/abap-mcp-adt-powerup/` (git origin `github.com/babamba2/abap-mcp-adt-powerup`). sc4sap project `vendor/` is an auto-generated dev-time clone that `bridge/mcp-server.cjs` bootstrap creates when missing — it is listed in `.gitignore` and does not participate in publish.

**Why:** 2026-04-22 incident. User had edited `project/sc4sap/vendor/abap-mcp-adt/src/` directly across multiple sessions, accumulating 37 uncommitted files on an outdated HEAD (`f21b342`) while the real source-of-truth at `marketplaces/abap-mcp-adt-powerup/` had already advanced 4 commits ahead (`d406628`) including a `@mcp-abap-adt/*` → `@babamba2/mcp-abap-adt-*` rebrand. The project vendor edits were orphans — some duplicated work already in marketplace HEAD, some never mirrored anywhere.

**How to apply:**
1. Edit MCP server code at `~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/abap-mcp-adt-powerup/src/` (that's a proper git clone — commit/push from there).
2. Mirror `src/` and built `dist/` into sc4sap's vendored copy at `~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/sc4sap/vendor/abap-mcp-adt/` for distribution.
3. Mirror from marketplaces/sc4sap into `cache/sc4sap/.../vendor/abap-mcp-adt/` to take effect in the running session (full replace if version gap — see `feedback_vendor_patch_version_check.md`).
4. Never touch `project/sc4sap/vendor/abap-mcp-adt/`. If it exists, leave it alone or `rm -rf` it — bridge re-clones on next bootstrap (~1 min, needs network).
name: abap-mcp-adt-powerup runtime path — bridge loads cache vendor, not marketplaces
description: When fixing abap-mcp-adt-powerup, dist build under marketplaces is NOT what MCP runs; you must mirror dist/ to cache vendor before restart
type: reference
originSessionId: 7d3a12fd-25da-4eb7-8ff2-ddc75a64b842
The sc4sap bridge launches `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bridge/mcp-server.cjs` which spawns `vendor/abap-mcp-adt/dist/server/launcher.js`. Under Claude Code, `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` resolves to:

`~/.claude/plugins/cache/sc4sap/sc4sap/<version>/` — `<version>` is the `installPath` in `installed_plugins.json`, see [[reference_sc4sap_source_locations]] (0.6.35 since 2026-10-14)

So the actual code path the running MCP loads is:

`~/.claude/plugins/cache/sc4sap/sc4sap/<version>/vendor/abap-mcp-adt/dist/`

NOT `~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/abap-mcp-adt-powerup/dist/` (which is the user's developer working tree / SoT for npm publish).

`SC4SAP_MCP_AUTOBUILD=1` self-heal logic in bridge/mcp-server.cjs only copies missing deps from marketplace vendor when production node_modules is broken. It does NOT auto-mirror dist/ on every launch. Stale cache vendor dist with fresh marketplace dist will silently keep running the OLD code post-restart.

After building any fix under `marketplaces/abap-mcp-adt-powerup/` (`npm run build:fast`), the workflow is:

1. Confirm `package.json` version matches between marketplace and cache vendor (per `feedback_vendor_patch_version_check.md`).
2. If match → `cp` only the changed `dist/**` files from marketplace → cache vendor. `diff -rq` both dist trees should be empty after.
3. Full Claude Code restart (per `reference_mcp_stale_password_env.md` — `/mcp` reconnect does not re-spawn the Node process).
4. Smoke test the new code path.

If you forget step 2, smoke test fails post-restart with the OLD code's symptom even though the SoT looks correct — exact pitfall hit on 2026-05-08 (rfcBackend lazy-resolution fix).
name: Vendor patch — diff package.json version first
description: When patching a vendor/ dist, diff package.json version between source and target before copying; on major gap replace whole vendor (node_modules included)
type: feedback
originSessionId: 0f8d75a1-19fc-415f-890e-3d9ef52c9de8
When syncing a `vendor/<pkg>/` between locations (project ↔ marketplace ↔ cache), **first diff `package.json` version**. Do not copy only `dist/` if a major version gap exists — replace the whole vendor directory (node_modules + package.json + src + dist + everything).

**Why:** 2026-04-22 incident. Cache vendor was at MCP server v4.5.3 (scope `@mcp-abap-adt/*`) while marketplace vendor had rebuilt at v4.8.0 (rebrand to scope `@babamba2/mcp-abap-adt-*`). A dist-only copy produced a broken state: v4.8.0 dist referencing `@babamba2/mcp-abap-adt-auth-broker` that v4.5.3 node_modules does not contain → runtime `Cannot find module`. MCP server refused to reconnect.

**How to apply:** Before any vendor copy/patch:
1. `diff <src>/package.json <dst>/package.json` → check `version` + `dependencies`.
2. If version matches: dist-only copy is fine (fast, small).
3. If major/minor gap or dependency rename: `rm -rf <dst> && cp -r <src> <dst>` (full replace). Expect 100s of MB.
4. After sync, verify by running the launcher/bridge manually with the right env vars and reading stderr — don't trust "UI reconnect".

**확인은 끝냈어요**
- 버전은 4.8.12이고, `main` 브랜치에 커밋 안 된 변경은 없어요.
- 밀린 패키지는 23개예요.

- 런타임 의존성: `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` 1.32.1, axios 1.20, fast-xml-parser 5.11, zod 4.6.7, js-yaml 4.3.2, pino 10.4, pino-pretty 13.2
- 개발 의존성: biome, jest, ts-jest, tsx, express, yaml 등

**일부러 뺀 것**
- 메이저가 바뀌는 패키지예요: TypeScript 7, inspector 2, js-yaml 5, commander 15, dotenv 18, lint-staged 17, @types/node 26

- 그 결과 `@parcel/watcher` 경로가 267자가 됐어요.
- Windows 긴 경로 설정은 켜져 있어요. 하지만 `cmd.exe`는 260자가 넘는 폴더에서 실행되지 못해요. 그래서 설치 스크립트가 `ENOENT`로 멈췄어요.

**해결 방법은 처음부터 다시 설치하는 거예요**
- `package.json`의 버전 범위를 먼저 올려요.
- `node_modules`를 지우고 새로 설치해요. 새로 설치하면 패키지가 위로 평평하게 놓여서 경로가 짧아져요.
- `node_modules`를 지워도 지금 돌고 있는 MCP에는 영향이 없어요. MCP는 cache vendor 사본으로 돌아가요.

네, `npm audit`으로 확인은 하는 게 좋아요. 다만 고치는 건 결과를 보고 정하면 돼요.

- **`npm audit`은 읽기만 해요.** 취약점 목록만 보여주고 아무것도 바꾸지 않아요. 제가 실행할 수 있어요.
- **`npm audit fix`가 실제로 고쳐요.** 하위 의존성을 허용 범위 안에서 올리고 `package-lock.json`이 바뀌어요.
- **봐야 할 건 런타임 의존성이에요.** axios, fast-xml-parser, MCP SDK처럼 SAP와 통신하는 쪽이에요. 백엔드에서도 치명적인 취약점이 하나 나왔어요.
- **개발 의존성만 해당되면 급하지 않아요.** jest, inspector 같은 것들이에요. 배포 패키지에 들어가지 않아요.
- **`--force`는 쓰지 않을게요.** 메이저 버전을 올릴 수 있어서요.

지금은 설치가 백그라운드에서 돌고 있어요(`ba0mwavb4`). 끝나면 알림이 와요. 그때 빌드, 테스트, `npm audit`을 확인해서 결과를 알려드릴게요. 고칠 게 있으면 `npm audit fix`를 실행할지 그때 여쭤볼게요.

두 번째 설치도 같은 오류로 실패했어요.

**원인은 jest 30.5예요.**
- jest 30.5에 `@parcel/watcher`가 새로 들어왔어요.
- 그런데 lockfile에서 jest 하위 트리가 1,513개나 깊게 중첩돼 있어요. ts-jest 29와 버전이 엇갈려서예요.
- 그래서 `@parcel/watcher`가 260자를 넘는 경로에 깔리고, 설치 스크립트가 실패해요.

**해결책:** jest와 jest-util은 지금 버전(30.2)으로 두고 나머지만 올려요. 둘 다 개발용이라 배포 패키지에는 영향이 없어요.

**주의:** 지금 이 폴더의 `node_modules`는 비어 있어요(설치 실패로 지워진 상태). 실행 중인 MCP는 cache vendor를 쓰니 영향은 없어요.

audit은 빼고, 아래 명령으로 설치·빌드·테스트까지 한 번에 돌려주세요:

```
! cd ~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/abap-mcp-adt-powerup && npm pkg set "devDependencies.jest=^30.2.0" "devDependencies.jest-util=^30.2.0" && npm install --no-audit && npm run build:fast && npm test
```

- 빌드는 `build:fast`로 해요. `build`는 biome이 `src`를 다시 포맷해서 상관없는 변경이 섞여요.
- 성공하면 제가 `package.json`과 `package-lock.json`을 커밋하고 `main`에 푸시할게요.
- npm publish와 sc4sap vendor 반영은 하지 않아요. 원하시면 따로 말씀해 주세요.

<!-- Fork of https://github.com/fr0ster/mcp-abap-adt — original project by fr0ster -->

# Changelog

## [Unreleased]

### Added
- **`GetSmartFormLayout`** (read-only, on-premise and legacy systems): page and window layout of a SmartForm. Per page the format, orientation, next page, CPI / LPI and style; per window its type (MAIN, SECONDARY, ...), position and size as stored (value + unit) and converted to millimetres (CM, MM, IN, PT, TW, and LN / CH through the page LPI / CPI). Reads the active version (a form that was never activated is read from its saved version and `active` is false). `language` takes a 1-character SAP key or a 2-letter ISO code. Layout only: no texts, code or form interface. Runs through `ZMCP_ADT_DISPATCH` action `SSF_LAYOUT`, so it works on the OData backend (BASIS 7.40) and over SOAP RFC (BASIS 7.31). Needs the new `ZMCP_SSF_LAYOUT` FM and the `SSF_LAYOUT` dispatcher branch; without them the tool answers with an install hint.
- **`GetSmartFormContent`** (read-only, on-premise and legacy systems): what a SmartForm prints, for preview rendering. Per page and window (position in mm) the content tree: text nodes with their lines (paragraph format, inline character formats, `&symbols&`), include texts, templates with line heights and cells (width, border widths, shading colour), loops and tables with header / footer events, graphics, addresses, print conditions; code nodes only as markers, never program lines. Also the form interface and global data with their types (`data`), the SmartStyles as CSS, SE78 graphics with a fixed key as BMP with their printed size, and include texts with a fixed key. Everything is written under the MCP output directory (`smartforms/<form>/`, full result in `<form>.content.json`); `summary: true` answers with an overview (windows, data declarations, `&symbols&`, graphics, files) because the full tree easily exceeds a tool answer. Runs through `ZMCP_ADT_DISPATCH` action `SSF_CONTENT` (FM `ZMCP_SSF_CONTENT`).
- **`RenderSmartForm`** (on-premise and legacy systems): the output of a SmartForm exactly as SAP prints it, for given interface values. Calls the form's generated function module with GETOTF (no dialog, no print, no spool) and writes the OTF and the PDF under the MCP output directory (`smartforms/<form>/<form>.sap.otf.txt` / `.sap.pdf`). `values` / `values_file` take the interface in internal format; `device` or `families` choose the device type, so the output has the printer fonts the form was made for. The form's own program lines run as in a real print and may read the database — pass invented sample values only. Runs through `ZMCP_ADT_DISPATCH` action `SSF_RENDER` (FM `ZMCP_SSF_RENDER`); without them the tool answers with an install hint.
- **`CreateSmartForm`** (writes, on-premise and legacy systems, DEV profiles only): creates — or with `overwrite` replaces — a Z/Y SmartForm from Form Builder XML (the format of SMARTFORMS > Utilities > Download and of `GetSmartFormContent`'s form XML). The form is checked and stored active, its function module generated (also for a replaced form); when the check finds errors it is stored inactive and the errors come back. `package_name` defaults to `$TMP`; another package needs `transport_request`. The XML travels raw-deflate compressed in parts of 5000 base64 characters, because the OData `Dispatch` function import carries its parameters in the URL. Runs through `ZMCP_ADT_DISPATCH` action `SSF_UPLOAD_XML` (FM `ZMCP_SSF_UPLOAD`); without them the tool answers with an install hint.
- **`DeleteSmartForm`** (writes, destructive, DEV profiles only): deletes a Z/Y SmartForm of a local package (`$TMP`, `$…`) with its generated function module — a dry run unless `confirm: true`; transportable forms are refused. Runs through action `SSF_DELETE_FORM` (FM `ZMCP_SSF_DELETE`).
- **`GetSmartFormContent`** reads more of what decides the print:
  - SmartStyle paragraphs and character formats as stored (value + unit, family, size, tabs), with the SE73 bar-code definition (`barcodeDef`: symbology, module, height) of bar-code formats.
  - Table / template patterns with their outer frame flag (`frame.border`), box sides switched on with thickness 0 (`on`), and the `reference` of a template line type that takes another line's height.
  - Styles named only in output options (template / window STDSTYLE) are read too.
  - The device type and its printer fonts for the form's families (`printer`).
  - Texts with no translation in the logon language are taken from the form's master language, as SAP prints them. This needs `ZMCP_SSF_CONTENT` with `IV_LANGUAGE` for the `FORM` part; an older FM keeps the logon-language texts.

### Fixed
- `npm run docs:tools` cut a description at the first quote of the other kind (`'… (e.g. "ZMY_FORM")'`, `"… dump's …"`): string values now end at the quote they opened with, escapes are resolved. The user-guide tool lists are regenerated with the full texts.

## [4.8.12] - 2026-10-14

### Changed
- **ADT source writes on BASIS < 7.40 now explain the invalid-lock-handle failure.** Some 7.31 systems never send a `sap-contextid` cookie, so no stateful ADT session exists and the lock is gone before the write: the PUT fails with HTTP 423 `ExceptionResourceInvalidLockHandle` in every session mode. No client-side setting fixes it. The error now carries a hint that ADT source writes cannot work on that system and that the source has to be edited in SE38 / SE24 / SE37. Applies to every tool error that mentions an invalid lock handle when `ABAP_RELEASE` < 740.

### Fixed
- **`ReloadProfile` switched the profile but not the connection.** The stdio server kept the connection context it built at boot, so after a switch every tool still talked to the previous system until Claude Code was restarted. A profile switch now rebinds the stdio connection context and drops the RFC sessions of the previous system (SOAP / OData CSRF session, native RFC pool, ZRFC proxy session). Every `SAP_RFC_*` key of the previous profile is cleared, so a profile that does not set one no longer inherits it. The default `MCP_OUTPUT_DIR` (`.sc4sap/work/<alias>/mcp-output`) follows the new alias; a user-chosen directory is left alone. When part of the switch fails, the result is `ok: false` with `restartRequired: true` and `errors`.
- **`ListTransports` / `GetTransport` returned nothing on BASIS < 7.40.** The ADT transport organizer does not exist there: the list URL answers an empty body, which parsed to 0 transports. On these releases the request header, tasks and objects are read from E070 / E07T / E071 with the standard `RFC_READ_TABLE` over SOAP RFC. No custom ABAP is needed.

# Changelog

## [Unreleased]

### Added
- **`GetSmartFormLayout`** (read-only, on-premise and legacy systems): page and window layout of a SmartForm. Per page the format, orientation, next page, CPI / LPI and style; per window its type (MAIN, SECONDARY, ...), position and size as stored (value + unit) and converted to millimetres (CM, MM, IN, PT, TW, and LN / CH through the page LPI / CPI). Reads the active version (a form that was never activated is read from its saved version and `active` is false). `language` takes a 1-character SAP key or a 2-letter ISO code. Layout only: no texts, code or form interface. Runs through `ZMCP_ADT_DISPATCH` action `SSF_LAYOUT`, so it works on the OData backend (BASIS 7.40) and over SOAP RFC (BASIS 7.31). Needs the new `ZMCP_SSF_LAYOUT` FM and the `SSF_LAYOUT` dispatcher branch; without them the tool answers with an install hint.
- **`GetSmartFormContent`** (read-only, on-premise and legacy systems): what a SmartForm prints, for preview rendering. Per page and window (position in mm) the content tree: text nodes with their lines (paragraph format, inline character formats, `&symbols&`), include texts, templates with line heights and cells (width, border widths, shading colour), loops and tables with header / footer events, graphics, addresses, print conditions; code nodes only as markers, never program lines. Also the form interface and global data with their types (`data`), the SmartStyles as CSS, SE78 graphics with a fixed key as BMP with their printed size, and include texts with a fixed key. Everything is written under the MCP output directory (`smartforms/<form>/`, full result in `<form>.content.json`); `summary: true` answers with an overview (windows, data declarations, `&symbols&`, graphics, files) because the full tree easily exceeds a tool answer. Runs through `ZMCP_ADT_DISPATCH` action `SSF_CONTENT` (FM `ZMCP_SSF_CONTENT`).
- **`RenderSmartForm`** (on-premise and legacy systems): the output of a SmartForm exactly as SAP prints it, for given interface values. Calls the form's generated function module with GETOTF (no dialog, no print, no spool) and writes the OTF and the PDF under the MCP output directory (`smartforms/<form>/<form>.sap.otf.txt` / `.sap.pdf`). `values` / `values_file` take the interface in internal format; `device` or `families` choose the device type, so the output has the printer fonts the form was made for. The form's own program lines run as in a real print and may read the database — pass invented sample values only. Runs through `ZMCP_ADT_DISPATCH` action `SSF_RENDER` (FM `ZMCP_SSF_RENDER`); without them the tool answers with an install hint.
- **`CreateSmartForm`** (writes, on-premise and legacy systems, DEV profiles only): creates — or with `overwrite` replaces — a Z/Y SmartForm from Form Builder XML (the format of SMARTFORMS > Utilities > Download and of `GetSmartFormContent`'s form XML). The form is checked and stored active, its function module generated (also for a replaced form); when the check finds errors it is stored inactive and the errors come back. `package_name` defaults to `$TMP`; another package needs `transport_request`. The XML travels raw-deflate compressed in parts of 5000 base64 characters, because the OData `Dispatch` function import carries its parameters in the URL. Runs through `ZMCP_ADT_DISPATCH` action `SSF_UPLOAD_XML` (FM `ZMCP_SSF_UPLOAD`); without them the tool answers with an install hint.
- **`DeleteSmartForm`** (writes, destructive, DEV profiles only): deletes a Z/Y SmartForm of a local package (`$TMP`, `$…`) with its generated function module — a dry run unless `confirm: true`; transportable forms are refused. Runs through action `SSF_DELETE_FORM` (FM `ZMCP_SSF_DELETE`).
- **`GetSmartFormContent`** reads more of what decides the print:
  - SmartStyle paragraphs and character formats as stored (value + unit, family, size, tabs), with the SE73 bar-code definition (`barcodeDef`: symbology, module, height) of bar-code formats.
  - Table / template patterns with their outer frame flag (`frame.border`), box sides switched on with thickness 0 (`on`), and the `reference` of a template line type that takes another line's height.
  - Styles named only in output options (template / window STDSTYLE) are read too.
  - The device type and its printer fonts for the form's families (`printer`).
  - Texts with no translation in the logon language are taken from the form's master language, as SAP prints them. This needs `ZMCP_SSF_CONTENT` with `IV_LANGUAGE` for the `FORM` part; an older FM keeps the logon-language texts.

### Fixed
- `npm run docs:tools` cut a description at the first quote of the other kind (`'… (e.g. "ZMY_FORM")'`, `"… dump's …"`): string values now end at the quote they opened with, escapes are resolved. The user-guide tool lists are regenerated with the full texts.

## [4.8.12] - 2026-10-14

### Changed
- **ADT source writes on BASIS < 7.40 now explain the invalid-lock-handle failure.** Some 7.31 systems never send a `sap-contextid` cookie, so no stateful ADT session exists and the lock is gone before the write: the PUT fails with HTTP 423 `ExceptionResourceInvalidLockHandle` in every session mode. No client-side setting fixes it. The error now carries a hint that ADT source writes cannot work on that system and that the source has to be edited in SE38 / SE24 / SE37. Applies to every tool error that mentions an invalid lock handle when `ABAP_RELEASE` < 740.

### Fixed
- **`ReloadProfile` switched the profile but not the connection.** The stdio server kept the connection context it built at boot, so after a switch every tool still talked to the previous system until Claude Code was restarted. A profile switch now rebinds the stdio connection context and drops the RFC sessions of the previous system (SOAP / OData CSRF session, native RFC pool, ZRFC proxy session). Every `SAP_RFC_*` key of the previous profile is cleared, so a profile that does not set one no longer inherits it. The default `MCP_OUTPUT_DIR` (`.sc4sap/work/<alias>/mcp-output`) follows the new alias; a user-chosen directory is left alone. When part of the switch fails, the result is `ok: false` with `restartRequired: true` and `errors`.
- **`ListTransports` / `GetTransport` returned nothing on BASIS < 7.40.** The ADT transport organizer does not exist there: the list URL answers an empty body, which parsed to 0 transports. On these releases the request header, tasks and objects are read from E070 / E07T / E071 with the standard `RFC_READ_TABLE` over SOAP RFC. No custom ABAP is needed.

name: sc4sap plugin — 3-location sync when patching
description: When patching sc4sap plugin code, keep project source + marketplace + user cache in sync (user is plugin author, publishes from project folder)
type: reference
originSessionId: 624e4d17-84e6-4cca-a52f-34db7cd7ad7e
User authors the sc4sap plugin. When patching plugin code (bridge, scripts, hooks, skills), THREE locations must stay in sync:

1. **Project source (distribution source-of-truth)** — `C:/Users/pssps/Documents/Projects/sc4sap_project/sc4sap/`
   - This is what gets published to the marketplace.
   - All new fixes MUST land here first (for git/CHANGELOG).
2. **Marketplace copy (install-time source)** — `C:/Users/pssps/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/sc4sap/`
   - What Claude Code ships into the cache when the plugin is enabled/updated.
3. **Cache (runtime)** — `C:/Users/pssps/.claude/plugins/cache/sc4sap/sc4sap/<version>/`
   - What actually runs. A fresh plugin install copies from marketplace → cache, overwriting ad-hoc patches here.

**Patching workflow**:
- Edit project source first.
- Mirror to marketplace (for install-time correctness).
- Mirror to cache (to take effect in the running session — otherwise user must `/reload-plugins` or restart).
- `diff` all three at the end — they should match exactly.

**Why not just cache?** Cache is blown away on plugin update. Project source drives git + publish; marketplace is the Claude Code-facing source.

**Related**: `bridge/mcp-server.cjs` previously only checked legacy `<project>/.sc4sap/sap.env` and `<plugin>/.sc4sap/sap.env`, missing the multi-profile path (`<project>/.sc4sap/active-profile.txt` → `~/.sc4sap/profiles/<alias>/sap.env`). Patched 2026-04-21 in all three locations to resolve via active-profile first, with legacy paths as fallback.

**Which `<version>` folder runs (2026-10-14):** Claude Code launches the folder named by `installPath` in `~/.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json` (user scope), not the newest-looking folder name. Until 2026-10-14 it pointed at `0.6.14`, whose *contents* had been synced up to 0.6.35 / MCP 4.8.12, while folders `0.6.32`/`0.6.34`/`0.6.35` were older or had no vendor. On 2026-10-14 it was renamed: `0.6.35` = copy of the running folder + HEAD `c4d5d21` overlay, registry now points to `0.6.35` (backups: `installed_plugins.json.bak-20261014`, `cache/.../0.6.35.bak-20261014`; old `0.6.14` kept for rollback). Mirror target = the folder in `installPath`; check it before every sync and after a version bump.

description: As of 2026-04-24 the sc4sap active branch accepts pushes from multiple sources (user's other sessions, automation, future collaborators). Force-push / amend-push / destructive rewrites are NO LONGER SAFE. Plain push only; rebase allowed only on unpushed commits.
type: project
originSessionId: 0f8d75a1-19fc-415f-890e-3d9ef52c9de8
**Changed 2026-04-24.** The `active` branch at https://github.com/babamba2/superclaude-for-sap is now a collaboration branch — the user confirmed at least two sources push to it (different claude sessions + potentially other contributors). Observed evidence: during the 0.6.11 work, origin/active received `894c5be Merge branch 'main' into active` from a paek-authored commit while this session was composing a local commit, triggering a non-fast-forward push rejection.

**Why:** the earlier assumption that force-push + amend was safe on active (treated as the user's personal dev branch) is now wrong; treat active with the same discipline as main.

**How to apply:**

1. **NEVER** use `git push --force` or `--force-with-lease` on active. If a push is rejected, fetch + rebase (for unpushed local commits) or merge (if remote commits need to be preserved).
2. **NEVER** use `git commit --amend` on a commit that has been pushed to active.
3. **Rebase is allowed only on unpushed local commits** — e.g., `git rebase origin/active` to linearize local work before first push is fine, since no one else sees those commits yet.
4. **The Entire-Checkpoint attach workflow (`entire attach <sid> --force` + `git push --force-with-lease`) is not used**. Attach now runs automatically at session start via the `SessionStart` hook in `~/.claude/settings.json` (`entire hooks claude-code session-start`).
5. **Direct pushes to main remain prohibited** — changes flow active → PR → main as before.
6. When a push is rejected with non-fast-forward:
   - `git fetch origin active`
   - Inspect `git log HEAD..origin/active` to see what landed
   - If local commits aren't yet pushed: `git rebase origin/active` + plain `git push`
   - If local commits have been pushed (shouldn't happen, but if it does): `git merge origin/active` + plain `git push`

**Release flow unchanged**: mirror project → marketplace → cache per `reference_sc4sap_source_locations.md`, then plain push. PR #38 was the last merge that assumed personal-branch mechanics; PR #39 onward treats active as shared.
name: Always verify locally before publish / git push / any public action
description: Default to local verification (npm pack + install locally, smoke test) before any destructive or public-facing action like npm publish, git push to main, marketplace release
type: feedback
originSessionId: 44e18665-d223-475a-83dc-c08cd0bfcd54
When offered a choice between "just ship it, unit tests passed" and "verify locally first (npm pack → install → smoke test on real system) then ship", the user **always picks verify-first**.

**Why:** The user is cautious about irreversible public actions (npm publish has ~24h unpublish window, git push to main can't be silently undone, marketplace release affects other users). Unit tests use mocks and may miss real-environment shape mismatches. User explicitly said "무섭다" (it's scary) when a git-push plan was laid out without a verification lap first.

**How to apply:**
- For any flow ending in `npm publish`, `git push`, `gh release`, marketplace release, or similar: insert a local verification step **first** and present it as the default path. Do not ask the user to "pick A or B" if one option is a verify-first path — propose verify-first and confirm.
- Local verification pattern for npm libs: `npm pack` in source → install tarball into the consuming project → rebuild consumer → smoke test in the real target system (e.g. actual SAP ECC) before publishing.
- Local verification pattern for git pushes: confirm branch state + remote state + diff against remote before pushing; for destructive remote ops (force push, branch delete, backup-and-replace), pause and explicitly enumerate what will happen.
- If the user is already stressed (e.g. "무섭다", "걱정된다"), acknowledge briefly and lead with the safer path — don't enumerate multiple options again.

## [4.8.13] - 2026-10-20

### Added
- **`GetSmartFormLayout`**

lines: - **`GetSmartFormLayout`** (read-only, on-premise and legacy systems): page and window layout of a SmartForm. Per page the format, orientation, next page, CPI / LPI and style; per window its type (MAIN, SECONDARY, ...), position and size as stored (value + unit) and converted to millimetres (CM, MM, IN, PT, TW, and LN / CH through the page LPI / CPI). Reads the active version (a form that was never activated is read from its saved version and `active` is false). `language` takes a 1-character SAP key or a 2-letter ISO code. Layout only: no texts, code or form interface. Runs through `ZMCP_ADT_DISPATCH` action `SSF_LAYOUT`, so it works on the OData backend (BASIS 7.40) and over SOAP RFC (BASIS 7.31). Needs the new `ZMCP_SSF_LAYOUT` FM and the `SSF_LAYOUT` dispatcher branch; without them the tool answers with an install hint.

- **`GetSmartFormContent`** (read-only, on-premise and legacy systems): what a SmartForm prints, for preview rendering. Per page and window (position in mm) the content tree: text nodes with their lines (paragraph format, inline character formats, `&symbols&`), include texts, templates with line heights and cells (width, border widths, shading colour), loops and tables with header / footer events, graphics, addresses, print conditions; code nodes only as markers, never program lines. Also the form interface and global data with their types (`data`), the SmartStyles as CSS, SE78 graphics with a fixed key as BMP with their printed size, and include texts with a fixed key. Everything is written under the MCP output directory (`smartforms/<form>/`, full result in `<form>.content.json`); `summary: true` answers with an overview (windows, data declarations, `&symbols&`, graphics, files) because the full tree easily exceeds a tool answer. Runs through `ZMCP_ADT_DISPATCH` action `SSF_CONTENT` (FM `ZMCP_SSF_CONTENT`).

# Changelog

All notable changes to **SuperClaude for SAP (sc4sap)** will be documented in this file.
Format follows [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/); versioning follows [SemVer](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## [Unreleased]

## [0.6.45] — 2026-10-20

### Changed — `smartform-from-pdf`

- Item lines are always a loop. The planner reports item candidates: lines whose columns repeat at a fixed pitch, also items of several lines, a reference line above the line of numbers and a freight line that fills fewer columns. Over free texts (no ruled grid) the new `textItems` puts the column header, the loop and the totals below it into one MAIN window, so the totals move down with the items; cells follow each text's alignment and grow beyond the sample's width, rows never get thinner than their line spacing.

# SuperClaude for SAP (sc4sap) — Development Rules

This file is the **index** of development rules — NOT a payload to preload. Detailed rules live in `common/` and `exceptions/`. Consult files on demand per [`common/context-loading-protocol.md`](common/context-loading-protocol.md) — 4-tier model: **Tier 1** global mandatory safety baseline (always loaded by every agent: `data-extraction-policy`, `sap-version-reference`, `naming-conventions`; `context-loading-protocol` + `model-routing-rule` are orchestrator-only, read by skills), **Tier 2** role-mandatory per agent group, **Tier 3** triggered reads, **Tier 4** per-task kit. Everything referenced below is MANDATORY for every sc4sap session (agents, skills, direct user requests, pipelines).

## Development Standards — References

| Topic | Reference |
|---|---|
| Naming conventions (Z/Y prefixes, module prefix, includes, FGs, tables, DEs, DOs) | [`common/naming-conventions.md`](common/naming-conventions.md) |
| Field typing priority (Standard DE → CBO DE → new CBO DE → Data Type+Length; never `LIFNR CHAR 10`) | [`common/field-typing-rule.md`](common/field-typing-rule.md) |
| Function Module source convention (inline IMPORTING/EXPORTING/TABLES in FUNCTION statement; no placeholder, no shadow locals) | [`common/function-module-rule.md`](common/function-module-rule.md) |
| SAP version awareness (ECC vs S/4HANA — tables, TCodes, BAPIs, patterns) | [`common/sap-version-reference.md`](common/sap-version-reference.md) |
| ABAP release awareness (syntax availability per release, never emit newer features than `ABAP_RELEASE`) | [`common/abap-release-reference.md`](common/abap-release-reference.md) |
| Clean ABAP coding standards (paradigm-split) | shared baseline [`common/clean-code.md`](common/clean-code.md) + one of [`common/clean-code-oop.md`](common/clean-code-oop.md) or [`common/clean-code-procedural.md`](common/clean-code-procedural.md) chosen from the Phase 1B Paradigm dimension; also pulls in `constant-rule.md`, `text-element-rule.md`, `abap-release-reference.md` |
| Procedural FORM naming (screen-bound suffix) | [`common/procedural-form-naming.md`](common/procedural-form-naming.md) |
| OOP two-class split pattern | [`common/oop-pattern.md`](common/oop-pattern.md) |
| Include structure (Main + conditional includes) | [`common/include-structure.md`](common/include-structure.md) |
| ALV display rules | [`common/alv-rules.md`](common/alv-rules.md) |
| Tabstrip screens (STRIP_CTRL + subscreen area + tab PUSH rows, `CALL SUBSCREEN` in PBO and PAI) | [`common/screen-tabstrip.md`](common/screen-tabstrip.md) |
| OK_CODE binding pattern (one TOP variable + screen NAME + PAI dispatch; never `CASE sy-ucomm`) | [`common/ok-code-pattern.md`](common/ok-code-pattern.md) |
| SPRO lookup protocol (consultant agents, IMG/Customizing) | [`common/spro-lookup.md`](common/spro-lookup.md) |
| Customization lookup protocol (existing Z*/Y* BAdI impl, CMOD, form-exits, appends — mandatory before recommending new enhancements/extensions) | [`common/customization-lookup.md`](common/customization-lookup.md) |
| Data extraction policy (blocklist rule, `acknowledge_risk` hard rule, refusal template) | [`common/data-extraction-policy.md`](common/data-extraction-policy.md) |
| Transport client rule (every `CreateTransport` must receive explicit `client` from `.sc4sap/sap.env` SAP_CLIENT — never an implicit default) | [`common/transport-client-rule.md`](common/transport-client-rule.md) |
| Blocklist (per-category table lists) | [`exceptions/table_exception.md`](exceptions/table_exception.md) (index) + `exceptions/*.md` section files |
| Industry business-context references (14 industries) | [`industry/README.md`](industry/README.md) + `industry/*.md` |
| Country / localization references (16 countries + EU common) | [`country/README.md`](country/README.md) + `country/*.md` |
| Active modules — cross-module integration matrix (MM↔PS, SD↔CO, QM↔PP, …) | [`common/active-modules.md`](common/active-modules.md) |
| Context loading protocol (CLAUDE.md is an index; every dispatch declares its minimal context kit) | [`common/context-loading-protocol.md`](common/context-loading-protocol.md) |
| Model routing (Opus for judgment / novel code; Sonnet for template + bulk writes; Haiku `sap-checker` fan-out for fetch / verify / detect) | [`common/model-routing-rule.md`](common/model-routing-rule.md) |
| Model dispatch mode (`auto` default = route per rule; `user-defined` = ask Opus / Sonnet / Haiku before each dispatch group; set via `/sc4sap:sap-option`) | [`common/model-dispatch-mode.md`](common/model-dispatch-mode.md) |

Before any work: verify `.sc4sap/config.json` exists and contains `sapVersion`, `abapRelease`, `industry`. Every recommendation, piece of generated code, and tool invocation must respect those fields.

## Critical Rules (summary — full text in referenced files)

1. **Custom objects use `Z`/`Y` prefix.** Full rules: `common/naming-conventions.md`.
2. **Match SAP version and ABAP release.** Never use S/4-only tables on ECC or syntax newer than the configured `abapRelease`. Full rules: `common/sap-version-reference.md`, `common/abap-release-reference.md`.
3. **Transport discipline.** Every change goes on a transport. Description format: `[MODULE] [Action] [Object] - [brief]`. Never release with syntax errors or inactive objects. Every `CreateTransport` call must receive an explicit `client` parameter resolved from `.sc4sap/sap.env` SAP_CLIENT (full rule: `common/transport-client-rule.md`).
4. **Activate after every change.** Run `GetAbapSemanticAnalysis` for syntax, then `GetInactiveObjects` to confirm no leftovers. Follow Clean ABAP conventions: `common/clean-code.md` (shared) + the paradigm-specific companion (`clean-code-oop.md` OR `clean-code-procedural.md`).
5. **Data extraction is gated.** Before any `GetTableContents` / `GetSqlQuery`: consult `exceptions/table_exception.md` and `common/data-extraction-policy.md`. Schema/DDIC (`GetTable`, `GetStructure`, `GetView`, `GetDataElement`, `GetDomain`) is always allowed.
6. **`acknowledge_risk` requires explicit user affirmative** (`yes` / `승인` / `authorize` / `approve` / `proceed` / `confirmed`). Ambiguous commands (`뽑아봐`, `try it`, `pull it`, `my mistake`) are NOT authorization. Per-call, per-table, per-session — never carries over. Full protocol: `common/data-extraction-policy.md` → "The `acknowledge_risk` Parameter — HARD RULE".
7. **Industry context matters.** For config analysis / business process design / Fit-Gap: load the project's `industry/<key>.md` (from `config.json` → `industry` or `sap.env` → `SAP_INDUSTRY`). If unset, ask the user.
8. **Country / localization context matters.** For tax, e-invoicing, banking, statutory reporting, date/number formats: load the project's `country/<iso>.md` (from `config.json` → `country` or `sap.env` → `SAP_COUNTRY`, ISO alpha-2 lowercase: `kr`, `us`, `de`, `eu-common`, …). Multi-country projects load every relevant file and flag cross-country touchpoints (intercompany, intra-EU VAT, transfer pricing). If unset, ask the user.

Enforcement: L1 agent instructions → L2 this file → L3 `PreToolUse` hook (`scripts/hooks/block-forbidden-tables.mjs`) → L4 MCP server upstream guard.

## Plugin Usage

### Skills (`/sc4sap:` prefix)
- `/sc4sap:setup` — Initial plugin setup + SPRO config generation (auto-invokes `trust-session`)
- `/sc4sap:create-program` — Full ABAP program pipeline (Phase 0–8) with execution-mode gate (auto/manual/hybrid) and parallel Phase 4/6; auto-invokes `trust-session` at Phase 1
- `/sc4sap:create-object` — Single ABAP object creation (auto-invokes `trust-session`)
- `/sc4sap:program-to-spec` — Reverse-engineer a program into a spec artifact
- `/sc4sap:program-to-manual` — End-user manual for one program: one HTML file, scenario steps on drawn screens with numbered callouts, check points, field reference, messages & actions, glossary, revision history; one step per A4 landscape page in print. Output `.sc4sap/manuals/<PROGRAM>-v<n>-<lang>.html` (auto-invokes `trust-session`)
- `/sc4sap:analyze-code` — Static code review (auto-invokes `trust-session`)
- `/sc4sap:compare-programs` — Business-angle side-by-side comparison of 2–5 ABAP programs sharing the same scenario but differing by module / country / persona (reader = consultant) → one editable, versioned HTML report (verdict matrix + *Differences only*, field differences, screens side by side, decision guide, English companion) `comparisons/<NAME>-v<n>-<lang>.html` under the profile artifact base (auto-invokes `trust-session`)
- `/sc4sap:config-to-document` — One module's configuration documented from the live system: IMG tree, per IMG activity the real table values drawn on an SM30-style screen, customer-changed rows with their transports, configuration checks, SAP IMG documentation, consultant notes written by the module consultant agent and reviewed by `sap-critic` → one HTML file `config-docs/<MODULE>/<MODULE>-config-v<n>-<lang>.html` under the profile artifact base. MM first.
- `/sc4sap:interface-mapping-spec` — Interface mapping specification as one editable HTML page in the classic template layout (cover, revision history, header, Source → Target grid with R / MAPPING, optional synchronous response block, conversion rules, extraction condition, field guide). SAP side read from DDIC / FM signature or, for new interfaces, from a `TABLE-FIELD` list or the module consultant's proposal; counterpart fields, DB types, conversion rules and scenario defaults proposed; in-page checks; versioned with English companion → `interfaces/<IF_ID>/<IF_ID>-v<n>-<lang>.html` under the profile artifact base
- `/sc4sap:smartform-preview` — Expected print of one SmartForm without a print program: `GetSmartFormContent` (form XML, SmartStyle CSS, SE78 graphics) → windows drawn at their mm positions with templates, loops (sample rows) and graphics; `&fields&` filled with invented sample values sized to the DDIC types; report of cut-off cells / windows → `smartforms/<FORM>/<FORM>-preview.{jpg,html}` + `values.json` under the profile artifact base. Read-only.
- `/sc4sap:smartform-from-pdf` — SmartForm from a PDF (or screenshot) of a printed form: `read-pdf` (texts / rules / images in mm) → `plan-form` (rules → templates, texts in the formats of existing SmartStyles — no style is created) → fields, item loops and interface decided with the user (`shape-form`) → `write-form` (Form Builder XML) → `CreateSmartForm` on DEV → `RenderSmartForm` → `compare-layout` score against the source page → `smartforms/<FORM>/` under the profile artifact base. Writes (DEV only).
- `/sc4sap:analyze-symptom` — Dump/error root-cause analysis (auto-invokes `trust-session`)
- `/sc4sap:analyze-cbo-obj` — Inventory a CBO package → save frequently-used Z objects to `.sc4sap/cbo/<MODULE>/<PACKAGE>/` for reuse by `create-program` / `program-to-spec` (auto-invokes `trust-session`)
- `/sc4sap:package-to-process` — Reverse-engineer a CBO package into an End-to-End Business Process document (Markdown): auto-detected TCode entry points → AI process grouping (PR→PO→GR→IR style) → per-process narrative + Mermaid flowchart + sequenceDiagram + step tables. Auto-chains `sap-stocker` if CBO inventory missing. Progress bar at each step. Output: `processes/<MODULE>/<PACKAGE>/process-<YYYYMMDD>-<lang>.md` under the profile-resolved artifact base (`common/multi-profile-artifact-resolution.md`), with `_state/` checkpoints for resume (auto-invokes `trust-session`)
- `/sc4sap:ask-consultant` — Direct user-facing Q&A with a module consultant agent (SD/MM/FI/CO/PP/PS/PM/QM/TR/HCM/WM/TM/BW/Ariba/BC). Auto-routes by keywords, answers against the configured SAP environment. Read-only (no writes, no row extraction).
- `/sc4sap:mcp-setup` — MCP ABAP ADT server configuration guide
- `/sc4sap:sap-option` — View and edit `.sc4sap/sap.env` (credentials, industry, blocklist profile, HUD limits)
- `/sc4sap:sap-doctor` — Diagnose plugin / MCP / SAP connection health
- `/sc4sap:trust-session` — INTERNAL-ONLY — session-wide MCP permission bootstrap; direct invocation is rejected

### Agents
- Core: `sap-analyst`, `sap-architect`, `sap-code-reviewer`, `sap-critic`, `sap-debugger`, `sap-doc-specialist`, `sap-executor`, `sap-planner`, `sap-qa-tester`, `sap-writer`
- Checker: `sap-checker` — Haiku, read-only fan-out worker (`scout` / `verify` / `detect`) that returns structured lines; the main thread dispatches N of them and one Opus agent consumes the result. Used by `/sc4sap:create-program` Phase 1A scout, Phase 4 verification, Phase 6 `detect-judge`; `/sc4sap:analyze-code` size scout, large-object detect-judge, evidence verify; `/sc4sap:compare-programs` facts extraction; `/sc4sap:analyze-cbo-obj` + `/sc4sap:package-to-process` stocking scouts.
- Discovery: `sap-stocker` — CBO inventory / where-used graph / reusable object cataloging (Sonnet, R/O SAP + R/W on `.sc4sap/cbo/`). Consumed by `/sc4sap:analyze-cbo-obj`, `/sc4sap:create-program` (CBO reuse gate), and module consultants via their `<CBO_Stocking_Delegation>` block.
- Basis: `sap-bc-consultant`
- Module consultants: `sap-sd-`, `sap-mm-`, `sap-pp-`, `sap-pm-`, `sap-qm-`, `sap-wm-`, `sap-tm-`, `sap-tr-`, `sap-fi-`, `sap-co-`, `sap-hcm-`, `sap-bw-`, `sap-ps-`, `sap-ariba-consultant`

### SPRO Config Reference
`configs/{MODULE}/` contains `spro.md`, `tcodes.md`, `bapi.md`, `tables.md`, `enhancements.md`, `workflows.md` per module. Consultant agents consult these + `common/spro-lookup.md` before IMG answers.

### MCP Server (mcp-abap-adt)
All SAP interactions go through the MCP ABAP ADT server (150+ tools):
- CRUD: `CreateClass` / `UpdateClass` / `GetClass` / `DeleteClass` (and every DDIC/runtime object type)
- Analysis: `GetAbapAST`, `GetAbapSemanticAnalysis`, `GetWhereUsed`
- Runtime: `RunUnitTest`, `GetUnitTestResult`, `RuntimeAnalyzeDump`
- System: `GetTableContents`, `GetSqlQuery` (gated — see rule 5/6 above)
- Transport: `CreateTransport`, `GetTransport`, `ListTransports`

1. **Custom objects use `Z`/`Y` prefix.** Full rules: `common/naming-conventions.md`.
